Red Lake Nation

Red Lake Nation has a distinct governmental history among Minnesota’s Ojibwe communities. Its official public timeline is a starting point for reading the Nation’s account of northern Minnesota history, land cessions, resistance to allotment and constitutional change. This profile treats that account as Red Lake’s own perspective and preserves its separate political path from the six-band Minnesota Chippewa Tribe.

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Land cessions and resistance to allotment

The Nation’s timeline describes Ojibwe movement into northern Minnesota, encounters with Dakota communities and the growth of Red Lake communities. It identifies the 1863 Treaty of Old Crossing with the Pembina Band and later land cessions under settler pressure. Its account emphasizes resistance to dividing the central reservation into individual allotments and the retention of tribal land control. Treaty texts, land agreements and title records remain separate reading tasks. The timeline’s legal terminology, acreages and descriptions of other peoples require comparison before being adopted as an independent regional land history.

Read the sources [1] Red Lake Nation

02

A separate path of government

The timeline explains Red Lake leaders’ decision to retain their own political organization rather than join the six other Minnesota Chippewa Bands in the 1930s. It then describes constitutional change in the 1950s, the first tribal election in 1959 and later development of infrastructure, schooling and economic institutions. This concise sequence introduces Red Lake’s own account of governmental continuity and change. It remains an undated overview, with a linked historical-photo video that was not played. The 2023 water-tower photograph is a separate, modern infrastructure view and supplies no evidence for the timeline’s historical claims.

Tribal History & Historical Photos — Red Lake Nation ↗

Publication: Undated timeline; current website footer not treated as publication date

Red Lake Nation’s own timeline describes Ojibwe community history in northern Minnesota, the Old Crossing treaty, allotment policy and Red Lake’s decision to retain a separate political path rather than join the six-band Minnesota Chippewa Tribe. Its chronology and historical characterizations are attributed to the Nation; individual claims need comparison with treaties and archival scholarship.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Read the page’s full visible 17th- through 20th-century timeline (lines 33–73). The embedded Red Lake Historical Photos video was not played; it is not counted as inspected.
